question: Why is action-fruit abandonment called renunciation?
premises: one who abandons action-fruit is called renouncer
true abandonment is equal performance without attachment or fruit-desire
inference: renunciation is fruit-abandonment in action, not total action-cessation
uncertainties: long fused compounds may hide internal sandhi
kaścitphalasaṃbandhaḥ may be any connection with fruit
plain_english: Since embodied beings cannot abandon all actions, one who abandons action-fruit is called a renouncer; true abandonment performs actions equally without attachment, aversion, or fruit-desire.
